Coordinates are Benin City (Wikidata Q320704), seat of the royal court where the brass-casting guild worked.

madeIn.name: Benin City (royal court of the Kingdom of Benin)

location.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
location.institution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York (Michael C. Rockefeller Wing)

object.description: A high-relief brass plaque from the royal palace of Benin showing a warrior chief in coral-bead regalia, flanked by two shield-bearing soldiers and smaller attendants, against a background incised with the river-leaf pattern. Plaques of this kind were cast by the royal brass guild around 1540–70 and nailed to the pillars of the palace. Benin's palace plaques and heads were seized by the British punitive expedition of 1897 and dispersed to museums and collectors; this one entered the Metropolitan Museum as a gift of Mr. and Mrs. Klaus G. Perls in 1990.
facts: Cast in brass by the lost-wax method by the Ìgùn Ẹ́rọ̀nwwọ̀n guild of the Oba's court, about 1540–70.
The British expedition of 1897 removed thousands of objects from Benin City; the British Museum alone acquired 203 plaques in 1898.
Height 47.6 cm, width 38.1 cm, depth 10.8 cm; the holes at the corners held the nails that fixed it to a palace pillar.
